evidence: Start (Incident Report, Summary): elevated latency and errors in BigQuery began on 1 April 2023 at 03:30 Pacific. End (Detailed Description of Impact): third impact window closed 3 April 2023 at 05:30 Pacific. Regions (Mini Incident Report, Regions/Zones): only the US multi-region is listed as affected.
notes: Only location is the Google Cloud multi-region us, which is not a region, so no region code and scope unclear. Publication date taken from the full Incident Report entry (10 Apr 2023 08:40 PDT). Three separate impact windows (1 Apr 03:30-05:14, 2 Apr 03:00-05:08, 3 Apr 01:20-05:30 PDT); start and end span all three. Cumulative impact stated as 8 h 2 min in the Incident Report but 7 h 47 min in the Mini Incident Report description; duration_min left empty because a start and end pair is given.

evidence: Start (Mini Incident Report, Customer Impact): packet loss hit users for about 70 seconds beginning 29 March 2023 at 12:35 Pacific. End (Customer Impact): elevated latency for a small share of users lasted until 31 March 2023 03:00 Pacific. Regions (Regions/Zones): connectivity from us-central1 toward us-east4 and us-east5 was affected.
notes: Publication date from the Mini Incident Report entry (31 Mar 2023 13:57 PDT). Status updates also say packet loss affected Identity-Aware Proxy and Identity and Access Management alongside Cloud Networking, so services_n counts 3; the Mini Incident Report itself lists only Google Cloud Networking. Updates give approximate packet-loss windows 12:30-12:40 and 13:40-13:50 PDT on 29 March. All network flows resumed full operation at 06:30 PDT and the issue was marked resolved at 06:35 PDT on 31 March, after impact ended.

evidence: Start (Mini Incident Report): incident start recorded as 16 March 2023 12:50 Pacific. End (Mini Incident Report): incident end recorded as 19 March 2023 09:24 Pacific. Regions (Regions/Zones and Description): overloaded front ends in us-east4 pushed traffic into us-east1 and us-east5, raising latency and errors.
notes: Publication date from the Mini Incident Report entry (20 Mar 2023 14:38 PDT). Header location list shows only us-east1 and us-east4; the Mini Incident Report adds us-east5. Impact was intermittent, during daily US peak hours (about 05:00 to 19:00 Pacific). The affected service is listed as Google Cloud Networking - Cloud Load Balancing, counted as one product. The resolved message is dated 20 Mar 2023 04:46 PDT, after the stated incident end.

evidence: Start (Incident Report, Detailed Description of Impact): about half of security policies went unapplied from 01:35 Pacific on 9 March 2023. End (Remediation and Prevention): service had fully recovered at 02:24 Pacific. Regions (Summary): the outage was confined to asia-southeast1.
notes: Publication date from the full Incident Report entry (20 Mar 2023 16:07 PDT). Header shows incident began at 01:30 PST, but the Incident Report and Mini Incident Report put impact start at 01:35 PST; the latter is coded. The resolved message gives 02:30 PST. Only Cloud Armor is named as impaired, though the header also lists Google Cloud Networking.

evidence: Start (Mini Incident Report, Impact Period 1): first impact period began 3 March 2023 at 10:40 Pacific. End (Impact Period 2): second period ended 3 March 2023 at 18:00 Pacific. Regions (Regions/Zones): location given as Global, and the description says the latency was worldwide.
notes: Publication date from the Mini Incident Report entry (6 Mar 2023 15:00 PST). Location is Global, so no region codes. Two impact periods (10:40-12:30 and 17:00-18:00 PST), cumulative 2 h 50 min; start and end span both. The earlier resolved message (12:20 PST) predates the second impact period.

evidence: Start (Mini Incident Report): incident start recorded as 3 March 2023 11:18 Pacific. End (Mini Incident Report): incident end recorded as 12:45 Pacific the same day. Regions (Regions/Zones and title): location listed as Global; instance creation failed worldwide.
notes: Publication date from the Mini Incident Report entry (7 Mar 2023 09:00 PST). Location is Global, so no region codes. The resolved message gives 13:07 PST, after the stated incident end.

evidence: Start (Incident Report, Detailed Description, Cloud Spanner): Spanner customers saw errors from 04:57 Pacific on 27 February 2023; the summary puts packet loss at 04:58. End (Detailed Description): impact window runs to 05:12 Pacific unless noted otherwise. Regions (location list and title): Global plus dozens of regions listed; title says services hit globally.
notes: Publication date from the full Incident Report entry (3 Mar 2023 10:25 PST). Scope global: location list includes Global and the title says global. Regions are the header location list plus us-central2 and us-east7 named in the detailed impact. Not coded: BigQuery Omni locations aws-us-east-1 and azure-eastus2; multi-region and dual-region locations us, nam3, nam5, nam7, nam9, nam11, nam12, nam-eur-asia3; and Cloud Build's prod-global. start_utc uses the earliest stated impact (Cloud Spanner, 04:57 PST); the Summary and Mini Incident Report give 04:58 PST. end_utc uses 05:12 PST from the Incident Report; the Mini Incident Report and resolved message give 05:11 PST. Service-specific starts (e.g. Cloud SQL and Memorystore data plane at 05:00) are per service, not per region, so region_starts is empty. services_n counts 28 Cloud services and 8 Workspace services with stated impact; Cloud Data Loss Prevention is excluded because the Incident Report says it had no user impact.

evidence: Start (Mini Incident Report): incident start recorded as 2 February 2023 06:20 Pacific. End (Mini Incident Report): incident end recorded as 09:42 Pacific that day. Regions (Regions/Zones and Description): control plane latency affected customers in southamerica-east1 only.
notes: Publication date from the Mini Incident Report entry (2 Feb 2023 13:43 PST). services_n counts Cloud Networking load balancing, Cloud SQL and Memorystore for Redis. The resolved message gives 09:32 PST, earlier than the stated incident end of 09:42 PST; the Mini Incident Report end is coded.

evidence: Start (Mini Incident Report): incident start given as 30 January 2023 00:10 PST. End (Mini Incident Report): incident end given as 02:45 PST that day. Regions (Regions/Zones and Description): configuration change failures were limited to asia-south1.
notes: Publication date from the Mini Incident Report entry (30 Jan 2023 12:17 PST). services_n counts Cloud DNS, Regional Internal HTTP(S) Load Balancers, Regional External HTTP(S) Load Balancers, L4 Load Balancers and Health Check as a Service. A status update gave a start of 01:07 PST and the resolved message gives 02:20 PST; the Mini Incident Report times are coded.

evidence: Start (Mini Incident Report, Description): sporadic instance-creation failures began 15 December 2022 at 18:30 Pacific. End (Mini Incident Report): incident end recorded as 20 December 2022 09:54 Pacific. Regions (Regions/Zones and location list): location given as Global, with 34 regions listed as affected.
notes: Publication shown as 20 Dec 2022 16:02 PST on the Mini Incident Report entry, which is 2022-12-21 00:02 in UTC; the UTC date is coded. Scope global (Regions/Zones: Global; title says global). Header says the incident began 2022-12-20 01:42 PST and updates said 00:00 PST that day, but the Mini Incident Report dates sporadic impact from 15 Dec 18:30 PST, reaching 100% failure on 19 Dec 16:00 PST; the report's start is coded. Resolved message gives 11:14 PST on 20 Dec, after the stated incident end. Only Memorystore for Redis instance provisioning through the console is impaired; a gcloud workaround existed.
